sources.title: Michigan State University Extension — How to Roast Any Vegetable
sources.access: Author/independent source packet reports primary reading on 2026-10-05; integration packet reuses that evidence.
sources.applicability: Primary extension guide: drying, spacing, tenderness and different rates by type/size. Method evidence only; no certification of the eight house formulas or their yields, oil ratios, glazes or exact clocks.

sources.title: University of Minnesota — Roasted root vegetables
sources.access: Author/independent source packet reports primary reading on 2026-10-05; integration packet reuses that evidence.
sources.applicability: Primary extension recipe explicitly varies roasting duration with vegetable type and size, and requires easy fork penetration. Supports rejecting a same-size/same-rate guarantee. Its formula is different and is not substituted.

sources.title: Reynolds — Parchment paper temperature rating
sources.access: Author/independent source packet reports primary reading on 2026-10-05; integration packet reuses that evidence.
sources.applicability: Manufacturer rates this product to 425°F. At 450°F use bare metal or suitable foil unless the actual parchment manufacturer rates it for that heat. At 425°F also check the actual lining instructions; no assertion that all parchment has one rating.

sources.title: FDA — Selecting and Serving Produce Safely
sources.access: Author/independent source packet reports primary reading on 2026-10-05; integration packet reuses that evidence.
sources.applicability: Primary FDA handling guidance: wash produce before cutting under running water, dry with clean material, and separate ready-to-eat produce from raw meat tools. Washing does not sterilize. Applies especially to spinach/herb finishes and linked meals.

sources.title: USDA FSIS — Leftovers and Food Safety
sources.access: Author/independent source packet reports primary reading on 2026-10-05; integration packet reuses that evidence.
sources.applicability: Primary USDA general leftover handling: prompt shallow-container refrigeration within two hours, 3–4 refrigerated days and 165°F reheating. Quality/crispness comments are editorial observations, not source-tested shelf life.
sources.narrowRecheck: Direct page returned 403 during packet preparation; official indexed USDA text and accessible FDA chill guidance corroborate scope.

sources.title: Food & Wine — Jamie Malone’s roasted sunchokes
sources.access: Author/independent source packet reports primary reading on 2026-10-05; integration packet reuses that evidence.
sources.applicability: Named primary publisher and independently recovered 045e5ba2 original agree on the missing roast oil, raw vinegar reduction and transfer/wipe before butter. The current four portions are retained; no exact publisher yield is newly imposed. Current chili bloom remains an explicit adaptation.

sources.title: King Arthur Baking — How to make brown butter
sources.access: Author/independent source packet reports primary reading on 2026-10-05; integration packet reuses that evidence.
sources.applicability: Primary author describes browning milk solids, removing butter before blackened bitterness and promptly transferring to stop carryover. Applied to visible butter cues; no fixed browning time or water top-up is imported into this vinaigrette.

sources.title: GialloZafferano — Roasted potatoes
sources.access: Author/independent source packet reports primary reading on 2026-10-05; integration packet reuses that evidence.
sources.applicability: Italian primary publisher establishes the general potato/rosemary oven-roast family and a parboiled alternative, with materially different formula and heat. Does not establish Roman household authorship or certify the current no-boil family formula.

sources.title: Just One Cookbook — Roasted miso garlic cauliflower
sources.access: Author/independent source packet reports primary reading on 2026-10-05; integration packet reuses that evidence.
sources.applicability: Primary author explicitly warns that miso sauce burns readily; her different oil/salt first-roast/late-glaze recipe is not this saved mirin/sesame/rice-vinegar formula. Supports a scorch check and rejects generic Japanese-household authenticity, not exact transfer of her timings, maple balance or broiler method.

sources.title: Bon Appétit — How to roast sweet potatoes
sources.access: Author/independent source packet reports primary reading on 2026-10-05; integration packet reuses that evidence.
sources.applicability: Primary author explains contact/turning multiple cut faces and variable tenderness; her different unglazed method is not a source for this maple formula. Applied to correcting skin-side-down/bottom-brown conflict and rejecting promised chip-like crispness. No formula or new heat target imported.

storageClarificationSources.title: FDA — Safe Food Handling
storageClarificationSources.access: Narrow primary page rechecked on 2026-10-05; chill guidance and leftovers temperature table read
storageClarificationSources.applicability: Other perishables within 2 hours/1 hour above 90°F, refrigerator 40°F or below, shallow leftovers; measured 165°F leftovers reheat. Does not establish acid preservation or recipe-specific shelf life.

storageClarificationSources.title: USDA FSIS — Leftovers and Food Safety
storageClarificationSources.access: Existing author/peer evidence reused; this narrow direct recheck returned 403. Official indexed USDA text corroborates hot-ambient limit, rapid shallow cooling and 40°F storage.
storageClarificationSources.applicability: General cooked leftovers, including cooked side dishes; retain current 3–4-day guidance rather than infer preservation from vinegar or sugar.

storageClarificationSources.title: USDA FSIS — Keep Food Safe
storageClarificationSources.access: Official indexed primary text checked on 2026-10-05
storageClarificationSources.applicability: Most cooked leftovers 3–4 days at refrigerator 40°F or below; no guarantee this kitchen met handling conditions.

storageClarificationSources.title: FDA — Selecting and Serving Produce Safely
storageClarificationSources.applicability: Perishable fresh herb/leaf finishes at 40°F or below and clean separation; not itself a 3–4-day cooked-side shelf-life source.

limits: Evidence establishes only the stated formula or mechanism/handling scope. No native identity certification, measured kitchen yield, shelf life, nutrition calculation or physical test is supplied.
Exact committed origins establish saved content; comparison sources do not confer authorship on anonymous formulas.
